findings.title: Strategy close kills the shared pool and later messages are acked unprocessed
findings.body: FixedQueuePool is created once on ResultsStrategyFactory and shared across strategies, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() (and terminate()) always call queue_pool.shutdown(). Arroyo closes the strategy on partition revoke/rebalance and then calls create_with_partitions again on the same factory. After shutdown, Queue.put raises queue.ShutDown. submit() catches that, and the except path add_offset+complete_offset without ever running the result processor. The new strategy's commit thread then treats those offsets as done and commits them. Every message after the first rebalance is acknowledged and dropped. The offset tracker is also not reset, so a new assignment can still commit offsets for revoked partitions.

findings.title: Graceful shutdown commits before workers drain
findings.body: close() sets shutdown_event and joins the commit thread before queue_pool.shutdown() drains and processes remaining items. The commit loop exits after at most one commit of work that already finished. Items still queued are then processed in OrderedQueueWorker during shutdown, complete_offset runs, and nothing commits those offsets. On restart Kafka redelivers them, so uptime results are applied twice (duplicate incidents/check-ins) on every deploy or consumer restart. join() also ignores its timeout and always calls close(), so Arroyo cannot bound shutdown time.

findings.title: Queues are unbounded, so there is no backpressure
findings.body: Each worker queue is queue.Queue() with no maxsize, and submit() always returns after put(). The class docstring claims natural backpressure when queues fill, but the consumer thread never blocks. If result handling is slower than intake, queued WorkItems (including full Kafka messages) grow without limit until the process OOMs. Because commits cannot advance past the oldest outstanding offset, consumer lag also grows and the member can exceed max.poll.interval and be kicked from the group.

findings.title: Offsets are committed from a background thread
findings.body: A daemon commit_thread calls the Arroyo commit callback every second. Arroyo invokes submit/poll/close on the stream processor thread and expects commit() on that same thread; the callback updates consumer offset state and issues librdkafka commits. Calling it concurrently with poll/submit can race the consumer's in-flight commit, raise, or commit a mix of offsets the processor thread is not currently assigned. Commit should be driven from poll() (or another call on the processing thread), not a side thread.

findings.title: Worker failures still advance the commit point
findings.body: OrderedQueueWorker catches every Exception from result_processor, logs it, and always complete_offset in finally. get_committable_offsets then treats the message as processed and the commit loop commits past it. The strategy docstring says offsets are committed only after successful processing. A transient DB or downstream error is therefore acknowledged and never retried, so uptime results are silently dropped. The same swallow exists in submit() when decode or grouping raises, which also marks the offset complete.
